LESSON: MULTIPLICATION (8

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.4: Multiplication (8
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Multiplication (8, part of Numbers in Grade 4 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: When can you use multiplication in real life? 2. 2. How can you create patterns involving multiplication?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. team up with peers to multiply two-digit numbers by multiples of 10 using number cards or charts,

2. team up with others to multiply up to a two-digit number by two- digit number with and without regrouping using counters and prepare a corresponding multiplication chart,

3. work with peers to estimate and work out products by rounding off numbers to the nearest ten with products not exceeding 1,000,

4. share tasks while generating patterns involving multiplication with products not exceeding 100 and prepare multiplication charts using locally available materials,

5. team up with peers to play digital games on multiplication. 1. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. team up with peers to multiply two-digit numbers by multiples of 10 using number cards or charts,
2. team up with others to multiply up to a two-digit number by two- digit number with and without regrouping using counters and prepare a corresponding multiplication chart,
3. work with peers to estimate and work out products by rounding off numbers to the nearest ten with products not exceeding 1,000,
4. share tasks while generating patterns involving multiplication with products not exceeding 100 and prepare multiplication charts using locally available materials,
5. team up with peers to play digital games on multiplication. 1. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Multiplication (8 together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and imagination: learner generatepatterns involving multiplication with a product not exceeding 100.

Values:
Unity: learner collaborates with others to estimate and workout answers by rounding off numbers to the nearest

ten with a product not exceeding 1,000.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Education: learner prepares multiplication charts using locally available materials.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate multiplication to square plot for gardening skills in Agriculture.
